memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Jacob also went on his way, and the angels of God met him. When Jacob saw them, he said, 'This is the camp of God!' So he named that place Mahanaim." - Gen 32:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As Jacob sets out toward home — and toward a dreaded meeting with Esau — God gives him a striking encouragement. The angels of God meet him. Jacob sees this heavenly company and exclaims, "This is the camp of God!" He names the place Mahanaim, which means "two camps." There was his own small, vulnerable camp of women, children, and flocks — and there, alongside it, the mighty camp of God.

What perfect timing. Jacob was walking into fear and uncertainty, unsure whether his brother would embrace him or destroy him. And just then God let him glimpse the unseen reality: he was not travelling alone. God's own host was with him.

We often forget that there is more around us than we can see. When the servant of the prophet Elisha panicked at an approaching army, Elisha prayed that his eyes would be opened — and the young man saw the hills full of God's fiery chariots (2 Kings 6:16-17). The unseen camp of God surrounds His people.

If you are heading into something frightening, remember Mahanaim. You may feel small and exposed, but you are not on your own. God's protecting presence encamps around those who fear Him (Ps 34:7). There are always "two camps" — yours, and the far greater camp of God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I remember that God's unseen presence surrounds me?
2. Where do I feel small and exposed, needing to see the "camp of God"?
3. How would facing my fears change if I trusted God was encamped around me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, open my eyes to the unseen reality that You are with me. When I feel small and afraid, remind me of the camp of God around me, and give me courage. Amen.
